requirements.statement: One graph-selected typed settings registry applies authorized transactions and persists values in their owning scopes.
acceptance: Client and headless derive the same authoritative effective settings snapshot.
Preview failure rolls back and user/world values survive through their authorized persistence paths.

requirements.statement: Every UI, CLI and API setting change uses one typed prepare, preview, apply and rollback transaction.
acceptance: Validation, authority, callback failure, cancel and preview timeout leave either the complete old or complete new effective snapshot.
Restart and world-reactivation impacts are reported without applying unauthorized partial changes.

requirements.statement: Device and user settings persist through a versioned canonical old-or-complete-new file protocol.
acceptance: UI scale, view distance and binding profiles survive process restart after successful apply.
Corrupt, newer and orphan values are diagnosed and preserved without silently overwriting user data.

requirements.statement: The shipped product defines a complete categorized settings catalog with stable ownership, defaults, constraints, scope, authority, apply impact and availability instead of relying on host-local controls.
acceptance: The shell and client-world projections expose every registered baseline setting and every rebindable input action through the selected surface provider.
Accessibility, Controls, Audio, Video, Interface, Gameplay, World, Packages and Developer have either explicit rows or an explicit feature-conditional or no-consumer explanation.
A product-entry journey changes UI scale, view distance, one audio value and one binding, observes preview or impact, applies, restarts and recovers the same effective values.

requirements.statement: Every logical package documents its user-configurable settings contribution or explicitly records that it has none, and every shipped setting has exactly one logical owner.
acceptance: Package documentation and the compiled registration image agree on setting IDs, owners, categories and availability.
Removing and restoring a package preserves its orphan user values without transferring ownership to the settings surface.
Composition parameters, new-world inputs, internal tuning constants and hard safety limits cannot appear as unauthorized runtime settings.
